proposals.before: From Kaiyuan to Xiande, fifty-three years passed—and through them the realm saw five dynasties.
proposals.after: From Kaiping to Xiande, fifty-three years passed—and through them the realm saw five dynasties.
proposals.reason: Chinese 開平 is the Later Liang Kaiping era, not Kaiyuan (開元).

proposals.before: From the Kaiyuan era through Xiande, fifty-three years in all—and through that span the realm knew five dynasties.
proposals.after: From the Kaiping era through Xiande, fifty-three years in all—and through that span the realm knew five dynasties.
proposals.reason: Chinese 開平 is Kaiping, not Kaiyuan.

proposals.before: Then Wang Chongzhi went with Cheng as deputy; Mo, Cheng, and the rest offered six Huai prefectures and a million a year in tribute.
proposals.after: Then he sent Minister of Rites Wang Chongzhi as deputy to Cheng with a memorial; Mo, Cheng, and the rest offered six Huai prefectures and a million a year in tribute.
proposals.reason: Chinese 王崇質副晟 means Chongzhi was Cheng’s deputy, not that Cheng was the deputy.

proposals.before: Then he sent Minister of Rites Wang Chongzhi with Cheng as deputy with a memorial; Mo, Cheng, and the rest all said Jing would cede the six prefectures of Shou, Hao, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai and pay a million a year to support the army.
proposals.after: Then he sent Minister of Rites Wang Chongzhi as Cheng’s deputy with a memorial; Mo, Cheng, and the rest all said Jing would cede the six prefectures of Shou, Hao, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai and pay a million a year to support the army.
proposals.reason: Chinese 副晟 makes Wang Chongzhi the deputy accompanying Cheng; the literal reverses who is deputy.

proposals.before: Mo and the rest saw Shizong’s martial brilliance was no match for Jing and the army was mighty and Shouchun near peril; they said, “We beg Your Majesty grant us five days’ reprieve to return and bring Jing’s memorial offering all north-of-the-Huai prefectures."
proposals.after: Mo and the rest saw Shizong’s martial brilliance was beyond Jing’s matching and the army was mighty and Shouchun near peril; they said, “We beg Your Majesty grant us five days’ reprieve to return and bring Jing’s memorial offering all north-of-the-Huai prefectures."
proposals.reason: Chinese 世宗英武非景敵 means Jing was no match for Shizong; the literal reverses the comparison.

proposals.before: Jing had ceded north Huai and sent Mo back; hearing Cheng was dead, he too posthumously made him Duke of Lu.
proposals.after: Jing had ceded land north of the Yangzi and sent Mo back; hearing Cheng was dead, he too posthumously made him Duke of Lu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 江北 is north of the Yangzi, not the Huai; the idiomatic mistranslates the ceded region.

decisions.reason: The era name is 開平, Kaiping. Kaiyuan would be 開元 and belongs to a different period.
The literal field also misreads 開平 as Kaiyuan instead of Kaiping.

decisions.after: The Chu Emperor of Later Jin posthumously made Jinzong General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.
decisions.reason: 出帝 is the title of Emperor Chu of Later Jin, not 'the Deposed Emperor.' Naming the dynasty removes ambiguity.

王崇質副晟 makes Wang Chongzhi the deputy to Sun Cheng; the old wording reverses the relationship and omits the memorial.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遣禮部尚書王崇質副晟奉表

decisions.after: Mo and the others saw that Jing was no match for Shizong's martial prowess, that the army was overwhelmingly strong, and that Shouchun was near peril; they said, “We beg Your Majesty to grant us five days' reprieve, so that we may return and bring Jing's memorial offering all the prefectures north of the Huai.”
decisions.reason: 非景敵 means that Li Jing was no match for Shizong, the reverse of the old literal translation. The revised English states the comparison directly and preserves the remaining clauses.
